content.text: The ownership architecture is uniformly in our favour. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: 13.1 IBM assumes and will assume ownership and MSL assigns and will assign all intellectual and industrial property rights for hardware, software, design and documentation of all Products delivered under this Agreement
input.rationale: The Agreement meets the preferred position and runs in our favour throughout. Section 13.1 (p0197) has MSL assign to IBM all intellectual and industrial property rights in the hardware, software, design and documentation of all Products delivered, and p0198 extends IBM ownership (with MSL assignment) to any invention MSL makes on Products or on IBM processes and systems, with MSL only retaining a use right for performing its obligations here — i.e. deliverables and work product vest in us with no joint ownership. Section 13.3(a) (p0208) expressly protects our pre-existing IP: nothing grants MSL any rights or licences in IBM's pre-existing IP except a royalty-free licence to use IBM confidential information under the AECI solely to manufacture Products for IBM, with any further licence requiring a separate signed agreement. Confidential information disclosed to MSL is returnable on demand (13.2(c)), and under the Loan Agreement Section 5 (p1530) IBM retains title to all Loaned Items with no transfer rights for MSL. On tooling, SOW 21.1(e) (p1105) confirms all tools, dies, jigs, patterns, equipment or Parts purchased, furnished, charged to or paid for by IBM become and remain IBM property; MSL's ownership of generic "Common Tooling" (p1088) is precisely the vendor-tools carve-out the playbook accepts. No provision assigns IBM IP, data or classified parts information to MSL, and there is no joint ownership. Two minor sub-elements worth noting but not flagging: there is no express licence-back of MSL background IP embedded in Products (mitigated by the breadth of the 13.1 assignment plus the bar on MSL using proprietary assembly/test processes), and there is no standalone "Customer Data" ownership sentence, which is unsurprising in a 1998 manufacturing outsourcing deal where information flows are governed by the AECI.
